title: Mohammed Bin Salman & The Rise of Saudi Arabia (English Listening Practice)
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 出品的《English Learning for Curious Minds》，在节目中，你可以聆听精彩的故事，了解世界上稀奇古怪而又美妙的事情，同时提升你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today it is the start of another three-part mini-series, this time on the making of modern Saudi Arabia.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们开始一个新的三集系列节目，这次的主题是塑造现代沙特阿拉伯。

sentences.en: In part one, today’s episode, we’ll be talking about the rise of the man behind it, Mohammed Bin Salman, or MBS, as he is often known.
sentences.zh: 在今天的第一集中，我们将谈论幕后推手穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼（Mohammed Bin Salman，也就是大家熟知的 MBS）的崛起。

sentences.en: In part two, we’ll turn to one of the most ambitious, almost science-fiction-like projects of the 21st century: a planned desert city of the future, 500 metres high and 170 kilometres long, called NEOM.
sentences.zh: 在第二集中，我们将聚焦21世纪最雄心勃勃、几乎像科幻小说一样的项目：一个规划中的未来沙漠城市，高500米，长170公里，名叫 NEOM。

sentences.en: And in part three, we are going to look at a somewhat darker chapter: the blood-curdling murder of the dissident journalist Jamal Khashoggi.
sentences.zh: 在第三集中，我们将探讨一个相对黑暗的篇章：异见记者 Jamal Khashoggi 令人毛骨悚然的谋杀案。

sentences.en: OK then, let's not waste a minute and get right into it.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们废话少说，直接切入正题。

sentences.en: If you went up to a random person on the streets of Britain and asked them to name as many British princes and princesses as possible, my guess is that they might be able to name a good chunk of them.
sentences.zh: 如果你随便在英国的大街上找一个人，让他们尽可能多地说出英国王室成员的名字，我猜他们大概能说出相当一部分。

sentences.en: If you stumbled across someone who was a serious royal watcher, perhaps they could name all 17.
sentences.zh: 如果你碰巧遇到一个狂热的王室观察家，也许他们能说出全部17个人。

sentences.en: In Saudi Arabia, however, I am pretty confident that nobody, not even the king, would be able to name every Saudi prince or princess.
sentences.zh: 然而在沙特阿拉伯，我敢笃定，没有人——哪怕是国王本人——能够说出每一位沙特王子或公主的名字。

sentences.en: And even if they could, it would take them several hours to list them.
sentences.zh: 即便他们能，也得花上好几个小时才能列举完。

sentences.en: There is no public list, but it’s estimated that there are anywhere between 5,000 and 15,000 princes and princesses in Saudi Arabia.
sentences.zh: 虽然没有公开的名单，但据估计，沙特阿拉伯大约有5000到15000名王子和公主。

sentences.en: Thousands of people with some claim back to the country’s founder, Abdulaziz bin Abdul Rahman Al Saud, or Ibn Saud as he’s commonly called in the west.
sentences.zh: 数千人都能追溯到这个国家的创立者 Abdulaziz bin Abdul Rahman Al Saud（在西方通常被称为伊本·沙特）的血脉。

sentences.en: He had almost 100 children, with a mixture of official wives and concubines, and most of them went on to have large families of their own, with each descendant having the right to call themself a prince or princess.
sentences.zh: 他有近100个孩子，分别来自合法妻子和姬妾，他们大多数后来都组建了庞大的家庭，每个后代都有权自称为王子或公主。

sentences.en: Now, the history of Saudi Arabia, even the relatively short history of the modern Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, is as fascinating as it is complicated, and we don’t have the time to go into it in detail today.
sentences.zh: 沙特阿拉伯的历史，哪怕是现代沙特阿拉伯王国相对短暂的历史，既迷人又复杂，我们今天没有时间详细探讨。

sentences.en: But for the purposes of our story, the thing to underline is firstly the size of the Saudi royal family, and secondly how succession works, how the title of king passes from one person to the next.
sentences.zh: 但为了我们故事的需要，需要强调的有两点：首先是沙特王室的庞大规模，其次是王位继承的运作方式，即王位是如何从一个人传给下一个人的。

sentences.en: In a typical monarchy — like Britain, Spain, or the Netherlands — the crown passes downwards, from ruling male to the eldest next eligible male.
sentences.zh: 在一个典型的君主国——比如英国、西班牙或荷兰——王位是向下传递的，从执政的男性传给符合资格的下一个长子。

sentences.en: From father to eldest son. And if that son has died, then to the grandson.
sentences.zh: 从父亲传给长子。如果那个长子已经去世，则传给孙子。

sentences.en: It follows a straight vertical line down the male line of the family, with some more forward thinking monarchies now allowing daughters to be considered as well.
sentences.zh: 它沿着家族的男性直系向下延续，而现在一些思想更前卫的君主国也开始允许女儿继承王位。

sentences.en: But Saudi Arabia was very different. When Ibn Saud died in 1953, he didn’t have one eligible son; he had almost 45 acknowledged sons, with the oldest in his 50s, and the youngest still a boy.
sentences.zh: 但沙特阿拉伯的情况大不相同。当伊本·沙特于1953年去世时，他并没有一个唯一的合格儿子；他有近45个被承认的儿子，最大的50多岁，最小的还是个男孩。

sentences.en: This created both a problem and an opportunity.
sentences.zh: 这既带来了问题，也带来了机遇。

sentences.en: The problem was that many of these sons were grown, adult men, with military experience, political authority, and powerful backers.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，这些儿子大多已经是成年男性，拥有军事经验、政治权力和强大的后台。

sentences.en: Choosing just one of those sons, or one of their children, would have meant favouring one branch of this enormous family over all the others.
sentences.zh: 仅仅挑选其中一个儿子或他们的一个孩子，就意味着要偏袒这个庞大家族中的某一个分支，而冷落所有其他分支。

sentences.en: And with hundreds of princes and thousands of descendants, that could have led to an immediate, and possibly violent, power struggle.
sentences.zh: 面对数百名王子和数千名后代，这可能会引发一场直接的、甚至是暴力的权力斗争。

sentences.en: But the flip side of this was that there was an almost 50 year age gap between the oldest and the youngest son.
sentences.zh: 但好的一面是，最大和最小的儿子之间有将近50岁的年龄差。

sentences.en: Saudi Arabia could adopt a different system that kept things in the same generation.
sentences.zh: 沙特阿拉伯可以采用一种将权力保持在同一代人手中的不同体制。

sentences.en: Instead of moving vertically — father → son → grandson — the throne could move horizontally, from brother to brother, staying within the founder’s generation for as long as possible.
sentences.zh: 王位不是垂直传递——父亲 → 儿子 → 孙子，而是可以在兄弟之间水平传递，尽可能长时间地保留在创立者那一代人手中。

sentences.en: So when Ibn Saud died in 1953, the crown passed not to one of his sons’ children, but to one of his adult sons: King Saud.
sentences.zh: 因此，当伊本·沙特于1953年去世时，王位并没有传给他的某个孙辈，而是传给了他的一位成年儿子：沙特国王。

sentences.en: When King Saud was removed from power, the crown passed to yet another brother.
sentences.zh: 当沙特国王被罢免权力时，王位传给了另一个兄弟。

sentences.en: And then another. And then another. For decades, power moved horizontally across a single generation—between the dozens of sons of Ibn Saud.
sentences.zh: 然后是又一个。再然后是另一个。几十年来，权力在单一的一代人中水平转移——在伊本·沙特的几十个儿子之间传递。

sentences.en: This was a deliberate decision. It kept the peace between branches of the family.
sentences.zh: 这是一个深思熟虑的决定。它维系了王室各支派之间的和平。

sentences.en: It rewarded seniority, experience, and age.
sentences.zh: 它奖励了资历、经验和年龄。

sentences.en: And, above all, it preserved consensus among a very large pool of powerful princes.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，它在数量庞大的强大王子群体中保持了共识。

sentences.en: But this was also something of a ticking time bomb.
sentences.zh: 但这也是一颗某种程度上的定时炸弹。

sentences.en: As time went on, and the founding generation began to age, the number of potential successors grew dramatically.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，创立者这一代人开始变老，潜在继承人的数量急剧增长。

sentences.en: Each of those sons had children. Those sons had children.
sentences.zh: 这些儿子们都有了孩子。这些孙子们也都有了孩子。

sentences.en: And all of them had opinions, ambitions, and networks of influence.
sentences.zh: 所有人都有自己的观点、野心和影响力网络。

sentences.en: The House of Saud was no longer a family tree.
sentences.zh: 沙特王室不再是一棵家谱树。

sentences.en: It was more like a dense, thick forest. And by the early 2000s, Saudi Arabia had reached a moment of quiet tension.
sentences.zh: 它更像是一片密不透风的森林。到了2000年代初，沙特阿拉伯迎来了静水流深的紧张时刻。

sentences.en: Everyone knew the horizontal model of succession couldn’t last forever.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，水平继承的模式不可能永远持续下去。

sentences.en: Eventually, the crown would have to pass down to the next generation.
sentences.zh: 最终，王位将不得不向下传给下一代。

sentences.en: And the next generation was huge— dozens upon dozens of princes who had grown up with extraordinary wealth, political connections, and varying degrees of competence.
sentences.zh: 而下一代规模庞大——有几十甚至上百位王子，他们在极尽奢华、错综复杂的政治关系和参差不齐的能力中长大。

sentences.en: Some were talented. Some were not. Some wanted reform.
sentences.zh: 有的人很有才华。有的人则不然。有的人渴望改革。

sentences.en: Others wanted stability. And many had spent their entire lives preparing for the possibility—just the slightest of possibilities—that they might one day rule.
sentences.zh: 其他人则想要稳定。许多人花了一生的大部分时间来为一种可能性做准备——哪怕只是最微小的可能性——那就是他们有朝一日可能会统治国家。

sentences.en: For the first time since the kingdom’s foundation, the question hanging in the air was not just who would be king next, but how that choice would even be made.
sentences.zh: 自王国建立以来，悬在空中的问题第一次不仅仅是谁将成为下一任国王，而是这个选择究竟将如何做出。

sentences.en: And it was into this world—a world of vast wealth, complicated family politics, and an increasingly urgent need for a younger, more dynamic leadership—that we find Mohammed bin Salman, MBS.
sentences.zh: 正是在这样一个世界里——一个拥有巨额财富、复杂的家族政治以及对年轻、更有活力的领导层日益迫切需求的世界——我们迎来了穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼（MBS）。

sentences.en: He wasn’t in the obvious line of succession.
sentences.zh: 他并不在显而易见的王位继承序列中。

sentences.en: He wasn’t the eldest son of the eldest son.
sentences.zh: 他不是长子长孙。

sentences.en: In fact, for much of his early life, he barely registered on the list of potential future kings.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在他早年的大部分时间里，他的名字在未来潜在国王的名单上几乎排不上号。

sentences.en: He was born in 1985, the sixth child of Salman bin Abdulaziz, a then 50-year-old senior prince who had served for decades as the governor of Riyadh, the capital city.
sentences.zh: 他出生于1985年，是萨勒曼·本·阿卜杜勒阿齐兹的第六个孩子，当时他的父亲是一位50岁的高级亲王，曾担任首都利雅得的省长数十年。

sentences.en: His father was respected, serious, disciplined — a man with a reputation for hard work and order.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲受人尊敬、严肃、自律——以工作刻苦和注重秩序而闻名。

sentences.en: But his father was only one of the almost 50 sons of Ibn Saud, and not at the very top of the succession list.
sentences.zh: 但他的父亲只是伊本·沙特的近50个儿子之一，并不在继承名单的最顶端。

sentences.en: It’s not clear exactly what number son he was, but it’s believed he was around number 25.
sentences.zh: 目前还不清楚他具体排在第几位，但据信他大约排在第25位。

sentences.en: So MBS, as the sixth son of a prince not expected to get anywhere near the throne, didn’t grow up expecting to be king.
sentences.zh: 所以MBS作为一个并非注定要接近王位的亲王的第六个儿子，在成长过程中并没有期望自己能成为国王。

sentences.en: He wasn’t educated abroad, like many of his royal cousins.
sentences.zh: 他没有像他的许多王室表亲那样去国外接受教育。

sentences.en: He didn’t spend his teenage years floating between luxury compounds in Europe or the United States.
sentences.zh: 他的青少年时期也没有在欧洲或美国的豪华庄园间游荡度过。

sentences.en: Instead, he stayed in Saudi Arabia, went to local schools, and lived a comparatively grounded life — well, grounded by the standards of a Saudi prince.
sentences.zh: 相反，他留在了沙特阿拉伯，上了当地的学校，过着相对接地气的生活——嗯，按沙特王子的标准来说是很接地气了。

sentences.en: According to a recent biography, as a teenager he showed little ambition or interest in climbing the royal ladder.
sentences.zh: 根据最近的一本传记，他在青少年时期几乎没有什么野心，也对攀登王室阶梯不感兴趣。

sentences.en: He preferred video games and McDonald’s to business and politics.
sentences.zh: 比起商业和政治，他更喜欢电子游戏和麦当劳。

sentences.en: Whether something changed, or he was silently plotting from a very young age, we do not know.
sentences.zh: 是发生了什么改变，还是他从很小的时候起就在默默谋划，我们不得而知。

sentences.en: But sometime in his late teens, slowly but surely, he started to make his move.
sentences.zh: 但在他快成年的时候，慢慢地、坚定地，他开始采取行动了。

sentences.en: He cultivated connections with businessmen, security officials, and younger members of the royal family.
sentences.zh: 他与商人、安全官员以及王室年轻一代建立了联系。

sentences.en: He developed a reputation for being the prince who got things done, who followed up, who didn’t disappear into luxury or lose himself in excess, something of a rare trait for a young, Saudi prince.
sentences.zh: 他树立了一种名声：办事雷厉风行、善始善终、不会沉溺于奢华或过度放纵，这在年轻的沙特王子中算是一种罕见的品质。

sentences.en: He developed a reputation for being serious, determined, and surprisingly focused.
sentences.zh: 他建立起了严肃、坚定且异常专注的声誉。

sentences.en: He studied law at King Saud University, graduating near the top of his class, and then began working informally as an adviser — first to his father, then to other senior royals.
sentences.zh: 他在沙特国王大学学习法律，以接近班级前列的成绩毕业，然后开始非正式地担任顾问——先是担任他父亲的顾问，后来又担任其他高级王室成员的顾问。

sentences.en: These weren’t glamorous roles. They were administrative, bureaucratic, and sometimes tedious.
sentences.zh: 这些并不是光鲜亮丽的角色。它们是行政性的、官僚作风的，有时甚至是枯燥乏味的。

sentences.en: But they were important. They gave him insight into how decisions were made.
sentences.zh: 但它们很重要。这让他深入了解了决策是如何做出的。

sentences.en: Who held power. Who merely appeared to hold power.
sentences.zh: 谁掌握着权力。谁仅仅看起来掌握着权力。

sentences.en: And where the weaknesses in the old system lay.
sentences.zh: 以及旧体制的弱点在哪里。

sentences.en: And here’s an important detail. Saudi Arabia is an absolute monarchy; it doesn’t run on political parties and elections.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个重要的细节。沙特阿拉伯是一个绝对君主制国家；它不靠政党和选举来运转。

sentences.en: It runs on networks, tribal networks, business networks, security networks, and all this underpinned by the sprawling network of the royal family itself.
sentences.zh: 它依靠的是人脉网络、部落网络、商业网络、安全网络，而这一切都以王室庞大的关系网为基础。

sentences.en: Knowing the right people — and being trusted by them — is one of the most powerful currencies in the country.
sentences.zh: 认识对的人——并获得他们的信任——是这个国家最有价值的资本之一。

sentences.en: MBS understood this instinctively. He also believed that his country needed to change.
sentences.zh: MBS本能地理解这一点。他也坚信自己的国家必须做出改变。

sentences.en: Around half the country is under the age of 30.
sentences.zh: 全国大约有一半人口在30岁以下。

sentences.en: Yet it was stuck in the past: ruled by men in their 70s and 80s, and beholden to conservative religious authorities that were given de facto power in the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 然而它却停滞不前：由七八十岁的老人统治，并受制于在20世纪80年代获得事实权力的保守宗教权威。

sentences.en: Criminals were still publicly beheaded, women needed male guardian permission for many aspects of life, and they weren’t allowed to drive.
sentences.zh: 罪犯仍然被公开斩首，女性在生活的许多方面都需要男性监护人的许可，并且不准开车。

sentences.en: Mohammed knew that something had to change for the country to modernise, but he must have thought that he would never have got the chance to have any say in it.
sentences.zh: 穆罕默德知道，国家要想实现现代化，就必须有所改变，但他当时肯定认为自己永远不会有机会对此有任何发言权。

sentences.en: This all changed in 2012, when his father, Salman, was appointed Crown Prince, in other words, next in line to the throne.
sentences.zh: 这一切在2012年发生了改变，当时他的父亲萨勒曼被任命为王位继承人，也就是王储。

sentences.en: And the then king, Abdullah, was rapidly approaching his 90th birthday, so this really was an imminent succession plan.
sentences.zh: 当时的国王阿卜杜拉即将迎来90岁生日，所以这确实是一个迫在眉睫的继承计划。

sentences.en: Suddenly, MBS was one of the sons of the next King, and he began to position himself right at the heart of the royal court.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，MBS成了下一任国王的儿子之一，他开始将自己定位在王室宫廷的核心位置。

sentences.en: Sure enough, in January, 2015, King Abdullah died, and the crown passed to Salman, MBS’s father.
sentences.zh: 果不其然，2015年1月，阿卜杜拉国王逝世，王位传给了萨勒曼，也就是MBS的父亲。

sentences.en: Now, Salman had other sons, but he made it pretty clear that MBS was his favourite.
sentences.zh: 现在，萨勒曼虽然还有其他儿子，但他明确表示MBS是他的最爱。

sentences.en: He immediately accelerated his son’s career, handing him two truly monumental positions that put him in control of both the money and the military: First, MBS was named Minister of Defence.
sentences.zh: 他立即加快了儿子晋升的步伐，交给他两个真正具有划时代意义的职位，让他同时掌控金钱和军队：首先，MBS被任命为国防大臣。

sentences.en: At just 29 years old, he became the youngest defence minister in the world, and within months, he launched a controversial military intervention in Yemen.
sentences.zh: 年仅29岁的他成为了世界上最年轻的国防大臣，并在几个月内对也门发起了极具争议的军事干预。

sentences.en: Second, and perhaps more importantly, he was appointed Chief of the Royal Court.
sentences.zh: 其次，或许也是更重要的是，他被任命为王室法院主管（办公厅主任）。

sentences.en: This made him the King’s official gatekeeper, controlling all access to the monarch.
sentences.zh: 这使他成为了国王的官方守门人，控制着所有人面见君主的渠道。

sentences.en: If anyone in the sprawling royal family or the government wanted to speak to King Salman, they had to go through MBS.
sentences.zh: 如果庞大王室或政府中的任何人想与萨勒曼国王对话，他们都必须通过MBS。

sentences.en: With this authority, he began his campaign to centralise power.
sentences.zh: 凭借这种权势，他开始了旨在集权的运动。

sentences.en: He started pushing the ambitious economic and social reform plan known as Vision 2030—a plan to remake Saudi society and end the kingdom's dependency on oil.
sentences.zh: 他开始推行宏大的经济和社会改革计划——“2030愿景”，这是一个旨在重塑沙特社会并结束王国对石油依赖的计划。

sentences.en: By promoting this radical vision, he positioned himself as the moderniser and the champion of Saudi youth, earning huge popular support.
sentences.zh: 通过推行这一激进的愿景，他将自己塑造成为现代化主义者和沙特青年的拥护者，赢得了巨大的民众支持。

sentences.en: But, and it is a big but, he still wasn’t crown prince; he wasn’t technically in line to the throne.
sentences.zh: 但是，这是一个很大的“但是”，他当时还不是王储；从严格意义上讲，他并不在王位继承序列中。

sentences.en: This title went to an older cousin, Mohammed Bin Nayef, or MBN for short.
sentences.zh: 这个头衔属于一位年长的表亲，穆罕默德·本·纳伊夫（简称 MBN）。

sentences.en: Now, MBN was a serious figure. He was the Interior Minister, a known counter-terrorism expert, and a favoured long-time partner of Western intelligence agencies, including the CIA.
sentences.zh: MBN可不是个简单人物。他是内政大臣，著名的反恐专家，也是包括中情局在内的西方情报机构青睐的长期合作伙伴。

sentences.en: He was the established choice to be the next king under the old system, a safe pair of hands.
sentences.zh: 在旧体制下，他是成为下一任国王的既定人选，一个稳妥可靠的人。

sentences.en: But in June 2017, King Salman made a shocking announcement.
sentences.zh: 但在2017年6月，萨勒曼国王发布了一个令人震惊的公告。

sentences.en: MBN was going to be removed from all duties, and MBS would replace him as Crown Prince.
sentences.zh: MBN将被解除所有职务，MBS将取代他成为王储。

sentences.en: Power was officially moving vertically —from father to son— shattering the seven-decade-old tradition of horizontal, brother-to-brother succession.
sentences.zh: 权力正式开始垂直过渡——从父亲传给儿子，粉碎了持续了七十年的兄弟之间水平继承的传统。

sentences.en: The transition was not exactly peaceful.
sentences.zh: 权力的交接并非完全和平。

sentences.en: Sources later revealed MBN was summoned to a royal palace late one night, held against his will, and pressured for hours to sign documents resigning his position.
sentences.zh: 知情人士后来透露，MBN在一个深夜被传唤到王宫，遭到扣留并被迫签下辞职文件数小时之久。

sentences.en: To show a facade of continuity, Saudi state television broadcast a clip of the newly appointed MBS kneeling to kiss the hand of the deposed heir, MBN.
sentences.zh: 为了营造一种权力平稳过渡的表象，沙特国家电视台播出了新任王储MBS下跪亲吻被废黜的继承人MBN手背的片段。

sentences.en: But the message was clear: the consensus era was over.
sentences.zh: 但传达的信息很明确：共识时代已经结束。

sentences.en: MBS had engineered a quiet, behind-the-scenes coup, consolidating power in a manner unseen since the kingdom's founding.
sentences.zh: MBS策划了一场悄无声息的幕后政变，以王国建国以来前所未有的方式巩固了权力。

sentences.en: And this was only the beginning. The next step in securing his absolute dominance was even more shocking: a royal purge that turned one of the capital's most luxurious hotels into a gilded prison.
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是个开始。为了确保其绝对统治，下一步采取的举措更加令人震惊：一场将首都最豪华的酒店变成镀金监狱的王室清洗。

sentences.en: On the night of November 4th, 2017, something extraordinary happened in Riyadh.
sentences.zh: 2017年11月4日晚，利雅得发生了一件非同寻常的事。

sentences.en: Without warning, dozens of the most powerful people in Saudi Arabia—princes, ministers, billionaires—received sudden orders to report to the Ritz-Carlton hotel.
sentences.zh: 毫无预兆地，数十位沙特阿拉伯最有权势的人物——亲王、大臣、亿万富翁——突然接到命令，要求前往丽思卡尔顿酒店报到。

sentences.en: Some thought they were being invited to an urgent meeting.
sentences.zh: 有些人以为他们是被邀请去参加一个紧急会议。

sentences.en: Others believed they were being summoned for an audience with the King.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则认为他们是被传召去晋见国王。

sentences.en: Instead, they walked into what was effectively the world’s most luxurious detention centre.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们走进了一个实际上堪称世界上最豪华的拘留中心的地方。

sentences.en: The Ritz-Carlton was shut to the public.
sentences.zh: 丽思卡尔顿酒店对公众关闭了。

sentences.en: Its phone lines were cut. Security forces surrounded the grounds.
sentences.zh: 其电话线被切断。安全部队包围了酒店四周。

sentences.en: And inside, some of the richest and most influential men in the entire Middle East were told they were under investigation for corruption.
sentences.zh: 在里面，中东地区一些最富有、最有影响力的人被告知他们正在因涉案腐败接受调查。

sentences.en: Among those detained was Prince Alwaleed bin Talal, the so-called Warren Buffet of Arabia, one of the most recognisable Saudi billionaires, a man with major shareholdings in big American technology companies.
sentences.zh: 被拘留者中包括阿尔瓦利德·本·塔拉尔亲王，被称为“阿拉伯的沃伦·巴菲特”，他是沙特最知名的亿万富翁之一，在许多美国大型科技公司拥有大量股份。

sentences.en: There were former ministers, media tycoons, heads of major companies, and even senior members of the military.
sentences.zh: 其中还有前部长、传媒大亨、大公司负责人，甚至还有高级军官。

sentences.en: In total, around 380 people were rounded up over the course of the purge.
sentences.zh: 在这次整肃行动中，总共有大约380人被捕。

sentences.en: They were held not in cells, but in the ballroom and bedrooms of the Ritz, sleeping under gold chandeliers and ordering room service under armed guard.
sentences.zh: 他们没有被关在牢房里，而是被关在丽思卡尔顿的宴会厅和卧室里，睡在金色枝形吊灯下，在武装警卫的监视下叫客房服务。

sentences.en: Officially, this was an anti- corruption campaign.
sentences.zh: 官方称这是一场反腐运动。

sentences.en: Billions of dollars had been siphoned off through decades of patronage, contracts, and opaque deals, and the government–or rather, MBS–said it was time to clean up the system.
sentences.zh: 数十年的裙带关系、合同和不透明交易吞噬了数十亿美元，政府——或者说MBS——表示是时候整顿这个体制了。

sentences.en: But almost nobody believed the official explanation.
sentences.zh: 但几乎没人相信官方的解释。

sentences.en: This wasn’t simply about corruption. It was about power.
sentences.zh: 这根本不只是关于腐败。这是关于权力。

sentences.en: By arresting some of the kingdom’s wealthiest and most connected figures, MBS was doing something unprecedented: He was removing every rival who could challenge him.
sentences.zh: 通过逮捕王国内一些最富有和人脉最广的人物，MBS在做一件史无前例的事：他正在铲除所有可能挑战他的人。

sentences.en: And it worked. Within a few months, detainees agreed to hand over assets, property, or cash in exchange for their freedom.
sentences.zh: 这一招奏效了。几个月内，被扣押人员同意交出资产、房产或现金以换取自由。

sentences.en: The Saudi state claimed to have recovered over 100 billion dollars’ worth of assets.
sentences.zh: 沙特政府声称已追回价值超过1000亿美元的资产。

sentences.en: But more importantly, Mohammed bin Salman emerged as the undisputed centre of authority.
sentences.zh: 但更重要的是，穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼一跃成为无可争议的权力中心。

sentences.en: The message was unmistakable. If he could detain princes and billionaires at will, there was nobody he couldn’t touch.
sentences.zh: 释放的信号毋庸置疑。如果他能随心所欲地拘留王子和亿万富翁，那就没有什么人是他动不了的。

sentences.en: And while the purge at the Ritz-Carlton made headlines around the world, inside Saudi Arabia it did something else: It made MBS wildly popular among young Saudis.
sentences.zh: 虽然丽思卡尔顿酒店的大清洗登上了全球各大媒体的头条，但在沙特阿拉伯国内，它产生了另一种效果：它让MBS在沙特年轻人中获得了极高的人气。

sentences.en: To many ordinary people, the old elite had lived above the law for decades.
sentences.zh: 对许多普通人来说，老一代精英几十年来一直凌驾于法律之上。

sentences.en: Suddenly, a young prince was taking them on—publicly, decisively, dramatically.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，一位年轻的亲王开始向他们宣战——公开的、果断的、戏剧性地。

sentences.en: It felt like a revolution, but a revolution led from the top.
sentences.zh: 这感觉像是一场革命，但却是一场由上至头发起的革命。

sentences.en: But popularity at home was only half the battle.
sentences.zh: 但在国内赢得人气只是成功的一半。

sentences.en: MBS knew that to truly transform Saudi Arabia, he needed to change how the rest of the world saw his country.
sentences.zh: MBS深知，要想真正改变沙特阿拉伯，他需要改变世界其他地方对这个国家的看法。

sentences.en: And that meant tackling the kingdom's greatest vulnerability: oil.
sentences.zh: 这意味着要解决王国最大的软肋：石油。

sentences.en: For decades, Saudi Arabia had been defined by a single resource.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，沙特阿拉伯一直被单一的资源所定义。

sentences.en: Oil paid for everything—the palaces, the welfare state, the military, the sprawling bureaucracy.
sentences.zh: 石油支付了一切费用——宫殿、福利国家、军队、庞大的官僚机构。

sentences.en: But oil prices were volatile, and MBS could see that the world was slowly turning toward renewable energy.
sentences.zh: 但油价波动不定，MBS看出世界正在慢慢向可再生能源转型。

sentences.en: He wanted to wean the country off its reliance on oil before it was too late.
sentences.zh: 他希望在为时已晚之前，让国家摆脱对石油的依赖。

sentences.en: He wanted to reshape the country’s entire economy, its international relationships, and—perhaps most ambitiously —its global image.
sentences.zh: 他想要重塑整个国家的经济、国际关系，或许也是最雄心勃勃的——他的全球形象。

sentences.en: He wanted Silicon Valley, Wall Street, and the world to see Saudi Arabia not as an oil state stuck in the past… but as the next great frontier for innovation.
sentences.zh: 他希望硅谷、华尔街和全世界看到的沙特阿拉伯，不再是一个深陷过去的石油国……而是下一个伟大的创新前沿。

sentences.en: He created a huge sovereign wealth fund, committing tens of billions of dollars to be invested in technology startups, pouring money into companies like Uber, Slack, WeWork, and DoorDash.
sentences.zh: 他成立了一个巨大的主权财富基金，承诺投入数百亿美元投资科技初创公司，向 Uber、Slack、WeWork 和 DoorDash 等公司注入资金。

sentences.en: In just a matter of a few years, Saudi Arabia wasn’t just buying football teams or luxury hotels.
sentences.zh: 仅仅几年时间，沙特阿拉伯就不再只是购买足球队或豪华酒店了。

sentences.en: It was sitting right at the table of global tech’s biggest bets.
sentences.zh: 它已经稳坐全球科技最大赌注的谈判桌前。

sentences.en: And it didn’t stop there. MBS struck personal relationships with world leaders, including Donald Trump, who visited Riyadh in 2017 on his first foreign trip as president.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此。MBS与世界领导人建立了私人关系，其中包括唐纳德·特朗普，他在2017年作为总统的首次出访就造访了利雅得。

sentences.en: Trump and his administration warmly embraced the young crown prince, announcing major arms deals, praising his reforms, and offering the kind of diplomatic support MBS needed as he consolidated power at home.
sentences.zh: 特朗普及其政府热烈拥抱这位年轻的王储，宣布了重大军售，赞扬他的改革，并提供了MBS在国内巩固权力所需的某种外交支持。

sentences.en: For the first time ever, it seemed as though Saudi Arabia was on the cusp of reinventing itself entirely—modernising socially, diversifying economically, and becoming a hub for futuristic projects.
sentences.zh: 有史以来第一次，沙特阿拉伯似乎正处于彻底重塑自己的边缘——实现社会现代化、经济多元化，并成为未来派项目的中心。

sentences.en: And perhaps the boldest of all these projects was one we’ll be talking about in part two of this mini-series: a new city in the desert, 170 kilometres long, built in a straight line, powered entirely by clean energy, and designed as a kind of techno-utopia for the 21st century.
sentences.zh: 而所有这些项目中最大胆的，或许正是我们在本系列第二集里要谈论的项目：一个建在沙漠中的新城市，长170公里，呈直线修建，完全由清洁能源驱动，被设计为21世纪的一种科技乌托邦。

sentences.en: A place called NEOM. But alongside this glossy vision of the future, there was a much darker side to MBS’s rule.
sentences.zh: 一个叫做 NEOM 的地方。但伴随着对未来的这种光鲜愿景，MBS的统治也有着黑暗得多的一面。

sentences.en: Because while foreign investors were flying in, and global leaders were shaking hands, opponents of the government—activists, critics, journalists—they were increasingly being targeted inside Saudi Arabia and abroad.
sentences.zh: 因为当外国投资者飞来、全球领导人握手言欢时，政府的反对者——活动人士、批评家、记者——却越来越多地成为沙特国内和海外的目标。

sentences.en: Women’s rights campaigners were arrested.
sentences.zh: 女权运动者被捕了。

sentences.en: Rival princes who had not been caught up in the Ritz-Carlton purge suddenly found themselves silenced.
sentences.zh: 那些没有在丽思卡尔顿大清洗中落网的敌对亲王们突然发现自己被噤声了。

sentences.en: Even tweets, at times, became grounds for imprisonment.
sentences.zh: 甚至连发推文有时也成了入狱的理由。

sentences.en: And in 2018, the world witnessed something so shocking, so brutal, that it permanently changed the international perception of Mohammed bin Salman: the gruesome murder of the journalist Jamal Khashoggi inside the Saudi consulate in Istanbul.
sentences.zh: 2018年，全世界目睹了一件如此令人震惊、如此残酷的事情，以至于它永远改变了国际社会对穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼的看法：记者 Jamal Khashoggi 在伊斯坦布尔的沙特领事馆内被残忍谋杀。

sentences.en: Now, we’ll be going into this in much more detail in part three, but in short, this well-known Saudi journalist went into the consulate, was murdered and then chopped to pieces with a bone saw.
sentences.zh: 我们将在第三集中详细讨论这个问题，简而言之，这位著名的沙特记者进入领事馆后被谋杀，然后被用骨锯分尸。

sentences.en: Although this was first denied by Saudi authorities, the official policy line is that it was carried out by rogue state actors, without the knowledge of MBS.
sentences.zh: 尽管沙特当局最初否认了这一点，但官方口径是，这是由流氓国家行为者实施的，MBS对此并不知情。

sentences.en: And for a brief period after this shocking discovery, it looked like it would be hard for MBS to come back.
sentences.zh: 在这场令人震惊的发现之后的短暂一段时间里，MBS似乎很难东山再起。

sentences.en: Businessmen who had once been happy to be photographed beside him declined meetings, investors pulled out of the country, and newspaper columns were filled with damning reports.
sentences.zh: 曾经乐于与他合影的商人们拒绝了会面，投资者撤出了该国，报纸专栏里充斥着 damning 的（罪证确凿的）报道。

sentences.en: But time and money were on his side. And, sure enough, investors, politicians, and celebrities didn’t take too long to change their tune.
sentences.zh: 但时间和金钱站在他这一边。果不其然，投资者、政客和名人们并没有花太长时间就改变了调门。

sentences.en: Saudi Arabia’s enormous wealth, its strategic importance, and its ambitious plans for the future proved too attractive for many to ignore.
sentences.zh: 沙特阿拉伯巨大的财富、其战略重要性以及雄心勃勃的未来规划，对许多人来说太具吸引力，以至于无法忽视。

sentences.en: Global CEOs quietly flew back to Riyadh.
sentences.zh: 全球企业高管悄悄飞回利雅得。

sentences.en: Tech investors resumed their courtship. Hollywood stars returned for glitzy events.
sentences.zh: 科技投资者恢复了追求。好莱坞明星们为了闪亮的活动而归来。

sentences.en: And governments—publicly or privately—re-engaged with the kingdom.
sentences.zh: 各国政府——无论是公开还是私下——重新与王国展开接触。

sentences.en: Within 18 months, MBS was hosting the G20 summit in Riyadh, where world leaders—including those who'd publicly condemned him—stood side by side with the crown prince for official photos.
sentences.zh: 在18个月内，MBS在利雅得主办了G20峰会，世界领导人——包括那些曾公开谴责他的人——与王储并肩站在一起拍摄官方合影。

sentences.en: And that brings us to today. As of the time of recording this episode, his father, the 90-year-old King Salman, is still nominally on the throne.
sentences.zh: 这就把我们带到了今天。录制这集节目时，他90岁的父亲萨勒曼国王名义上仍然在位。

sentences.en: Today, Mohammed bin Salman is not just the Crown Prince; he is the de facto ruler of Saudi Arabia.
sentences.zh: 今天，穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼不仅是王储；他已经是沙特阿拉伯的实际统治者。

sentences.en: When he becomes king, and perhaps he already will be by the time you listen to this, it will merely be a formality.
sentences.zh: 当他成为国王时，也许等你听到这里时他已经登基了，那也只是一种形式。

sentences.en: He already oversees everything from oil strategy to social reforms, from foreign policy to football clubs.
sentences.zh: 他已经监督着从石油战略到社会改革、从外交政策到足球俱乐部的一切事务。

sentences.en: He has relaxed some long-standing restrictions—women can now drive, cinemas have reopened, concerts are allowed, and the infamous secret police have been stripped of much of their power.
sentences.zh: 他放松了一些长期存在的限制——女性现在可以开车了，电影院重新开业了，音乐会得到了允许，臭名昭著的宗教警察也被剥夺了大部分权力。

sentences.en: For young Saudis who grew up unable to go to a cinema, or lived in fear of being stopped on the street by the religious police, these changes felt revolutionary.
sentences.zh: 对于那些在成长过程中无法去电影院，或者生活在害怕被宗教警察在街头拦下的恐惧中的沙特年轻人来说，这些改变感觉具有革命性。

sentences.en: Yet the darker sides of his rule remain impossible to ignore: the silencing of critics, the imprisonment of activists, the ongoing humanitarian crisis in Yemen, and the unresolved questions around the murder of Jamal Khashoggi.
sentences.zh: 然而，他统治中较黑暗的一面依然无法忽视：对批评人士的禁声、对活动人士的监禁、也门持续的人道主义危机，以及围绕 Jamal Khashoggi 谋杀案尚未解决的疑问。

sentences.en: To some, MBS is a visionary moderniser. To others, a ruthless authoritarian.
sentences.zh: 在某些人眼里，MBS是一位富有远见的现代化主义者。在其他人眼里，他是一个冷酷的独裁者。

sentences.en: To many, he is both. He is only 40 years old, and in all likelihood will look forward to the best part of 50 years on the throne of Saudi Arabia.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，他两者皆是。他今年只有40岁，按所有概率推算，他有望在沙特王位上度过最好的50年时光。

sentences.en: What is certain is that he is someone you cannot ignore.
sentences.zh: 可以确定的是，他是一个你无法忽视的人。

sentences.en: OK, then, that is it for today's episode on Mohammed Bin Salman.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天关于穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼的节目就到这里。

sentences.en: As always, I would love to know what you thought of this episode.
sentences.zh: 和往常一样，我很想知道你对这期节目的看法。

sentences.en: We have lots of listeners from Saudi Arabia, so let me know what you think?
sentences.zh: 我们有很多来自沙特阿拉伯的听众，所以请告诉我你们的感想如何？

sentences.en: How has MBS changed the country, and what hopes do you have for the future?
sentences.zh: MBS是如何改变这个国家的，你对未来有什么期许？

sentences.en: You can head right into our community forum, which is at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接访问我们的社区论坛，网址是 community.leonardoenglish.com，与其他充满好奇心的人一起畅聊。

sentences.en: And as a final reminder, this is part one of a three-part mini-series.
sentences.zh: 最后提醒一下，这是三集系列节目的第一集。

sentences.en: Next up, in part two, we’ll be looking at the astronomically ambitious and expensive project of NEOM, and in part three it’ll be the gruesome murder of Jamal Khashoggi.
sentences.zh: 接下来，在第二集中，我们将探讨 NEOM 这个天文数字般雄心勃勃且昂贵的项目，而在第三集中，我们将探讨 Jamal Khashoggi 惨遭谋杀的事件。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你刚才收听的是由 Leonardo English 出品的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，祝你一切平安，我们下期节目再见。
